reason: Head *h₁ed- exact in three branches (AVŚ 8.6.23 adanti, Il. 22.347 ἔδμεναι athematic, Vǫlsungakviða in forna 9 eta; all checked) with *kréwh₂s as its object in Vedic and Greek (kravíḥ, κρέα; exact, both < *kréwh₂s) and āmá- = ὠμός exact. Caveats: the full triad stands in one clause only in Il. 22.347 (AGDT tags ὤμ' attributive to κρέα, not predicative as the note says); in the AV āmám agrees with māṃsám and kravíḥ is the object of a second relative clause under the same adanti; RV 1.162.10 has āmásya kravíṣaḥ verbless in a horse-sacrifice (not savage) context; ON gives only eta + hrátt (a *krewh₂- derivative in the 'raw' slot), noun renewed (kjöt). Finite 3pl rests on the AV alone. West p. 80 claims only the compound *ōmo- + *ed- (ὠμηστής = āmā́d-); the free clause is the 8c extension, carried past P5 by the matching savage/demonic contexts.

Head *wes- is shared only at root level: Ved. root present middle (vastām RV 6.75.18, vásānām AVŚ 9.1.1), Gk active s-aorist (ἕσσον/ἕσσε/ἕσσαν, Il. 16.670, 16.680, Od. 24.59, Hymn. Hom. 6.6; all checked). The engine's nasal present wesnudʰí stands in neither passage, and the active voice follows Greek against the Vedic middle. *n̥mr̥tó- is exact but syntactically different: in Greek it is attributive to εἵματα (the head of the stock half-line περὶ δ' ἄμβροτα εἵματα ἕσσε, which Vedic lacks); in Vedic it is the substantivized covering (instr. RV, acc. AV). The instrumental follows one Vedic passage only; the object 'him' is interpolated. No scholarly claim links the Vedic and Greek phrases (West n. 126 treats ἄμβροτα εἵματα as Greek-internal).

Overclaimed third branch. OE swētne medo (Finnsburh 39) is a conjecture: Grein's apparatus records Hickes's transcript as hwitne ('white'), with svêtne credited to Ettmüller; the Gutenberg text prints the emendation silently, so 'checked' verified an editor's reading, not an attestation. The Ved/Gk core is good: *swéh₂du médʰu, both members exact and same formation (svādú- = ἡδύς, mádhu- = μέθυ), named by West ch. 2; RV 1.84.10 (svādóḥ and mádhvaḥ in separate pādas, partitive gen.; the only RV stanza with the pair) and Od. 9.162, 17.533 checked. Interpolated copula is the accepted NP-formula pattern. Drop OE or mark it conjectural and the line is sound on two branches.

Both words exact and checked (AVŚ 13.1.24 áśvāḥ … amṛ́tāḥ; Il. 16.380-381 = 16.866-867 ἵπποι | ἄμβροτοι, one couplet repeated), but the pair is generic (P5; cf. r2 dawn-sun-009): amṛ́ta-/ἄμβροτος is the stock epithet of anything divine, RV has no áśva- + amṛ́ta- NP (full sweep), and the Vedic is one late AV passage where amṛ́tāḥ is appositive (Greek attributive); the line makes it predicative with an interpolated copula. The only scholarly claim is motif-level (West ch. 3 n. 127); its Avestan witness Yt. 10.125 has auruuaṇtō … anaōšā̊ŋhō (checked in CAB, YtMihr32.3), neither word cognate. Durante 1976 (not held) is the only place a lexical claim could live. At the reject edge.

Object *wékʷos exact (vácas- = ἔπος, neuter s-stem) and the 'god hears my word(s)' context matches; both sides are formulaic in their own tradition (śr̥ṇavad vácāṃsi me RV 10.66.11c, 1.145.3b, pl. 10.65.13c; ἐμὸν ἔπος ἔκλυες Il. 16.236 = 14.234; all checked). But the head *ḱlew- is shared only at root level: nasal-present subjunctive śr̥ṇavat against thematic aorist indicative ἔκλυες, which the note says honestly. Number (pl. vs sg.) and possessor (enclitic me vs adjective ἐμόν) also follow Vedic only. Weak by the head rule, the strongest root-level case in the batch; the Pind. I. 6 exclusion is correct.
